title: Seat liveness leaf: a silence-vs-absolute-cap decider and a Windows process-tree/CPU probe, where an unobservable seat is never killed for silence
description:
LEAF split out of task-8f653d86bb4f445cb7ee358c5559f99a ("The seat timeout is a wall-clock cap from spawn, not a liveness test") by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18, because the whole fix measured at 11 files against the 10-file cap. That row is the CONSUMER and declares dependsOn on this one; it wires what this row builds into agent-spawner.ts, adds the absolute-cap knob, the moe start env roster and the docs. THIS row lands a pure module and its tests only, and touches no existing production file.

WHY IT EXISTS (measured live on UnAI 2026-09-18, and at HEAD). agent-spawner.ts:399-402 arms `setTimeout(beginTermination, timeoutMs)` once at spawn and never rearms it, so a seat is killed at MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS however busy it is. The quiet notice at :404-414 cannot help: the seat is `claude -p` WITHOUT --output-format, which writes nothing until it finishes, so every seat shows "0 bytes seen" for its whole life. Node 5 (15f56b77) was at minute 26 with a live bash.exe tool child started 60 s earlier (claude.exe cpu 25 s) and was on course to be killed at minute 30 mid-work.

WHY NOT STREAM OUTPUT INSTEAD. The parent row allows either streaming (`--output-format stream-json`) or a process probe. Streaming is REJECTED: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-exit-classifier.ts pattern-matches the seat's TEXT to detect provider limits, with regexes measured against specific claude.exe builds (`/You've hit your usage limit(?![.\w])/iu`, the 429 banner), and its own comment at :58 warns that a seat printing "rate limit" inside its JSON output must NOT park the provider. Routing everything the model says through JSON events risks a seat whose model merely writes "rate limit" in a code comment falsely pausing the whole fleet's provider. A process probe changes no output format and leaves the classifier untouched.

THE TWO LOAD-BEARING FACTS the design must honour:
1. THE SEAT ROOT IS A SHELL, NOT THE PROVIDER. On Windows the seat is spawned through cmd.exe (governor observed cmd pid 49960 -> claude.exe 17324). So "a live descendant exists", measured from the spawned pid, is ALWAYS true while the seat runs, because the provider process itself is that descendant. A tool child must be counted STRICTLY BELOW the provider process. CPU progress summed over the whole tree is the more robust signal and must be honoured independently.
2. ONLY POSITIVELY OBSERVED SILENCE MAY KILL (epic rail 4: unverifiable evidence gains no authority). A probe that fails, times out, or has no implementation for the platform reports UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN never earns a silence kill; only the absolute cap applies then. Without this rule, silent `claude -p` seats on any platform without a probe would be killed SOONER than today.

CONTRACT this row must export (the consumer row plans against these exact names; changing them requires amending task-8f653d86):
- `SeatLivenessSample` = { kind: "OBSERVED"; cpuMs: number; toolChildren: readonly { pid: number; command: string }[] } | { kind: "UNKNOWN"; reason: string }
- `SeatProbe` = (seatPid: number) => Promise<SeatLivenessSample>
- `SeatLivenessVerdict` = { kind: "CONTINUE" } | { kind: "KILL_SILENT"; silentMs: number; lastActivity: string | null } | { kind: "KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP"; ageMs: number; lastActivity: string | null }
- `createSeatLivenessTracker({ startedAtMs, silenceMs, maxRuntimeMs })` returning { noteOutput(nowMs), noteSample(nowMs, sample), verdict(nowMs) } — ALL liveness state lives here so the 480-line spawner stays thin.
- `createWindowsSeatProbe(run?: RuntimeCommand)` — one Get-CimInstance Win32_Process query per call behind an injectable runner, following apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-broker-identity.ts:14/:38 (the `RuntimeCommand` seam and `runPowerShell`).

OUT OF SCOPE: agent-spawner.ts, the knobs, the env roster, the docs (task-8f653d86 owns them); a POSIX probe (follow-up — on a platform with no probe a stuck seat now lives until the absolute cap instead of 30 min, which is the deliberate cost of never killing a seat on unverifiable evidence).
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts exports the exact contract named in the description (SeatLivenessSample, SeatProbe, SeatLivenessVerdict, createSeatLivenessTracker, createWindowsSeatProbe) with its one-line .js bridge beside it, and the file stays at or under 250 lines.

The tracker never returns KILL_SILENT unless silence was POSITIVELY observed: an arm feeds only UNKNOWN samples past the silence window and asserts verdict kind CONTINUE, then past the absolute cap asserts KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP; a second arm feeds OBSERVED samples with no CPU progress, no tool child and no output past the window and asserts KILL_SILENT with the exact silentMs. Reason codes asserted by value, never merely 'not CONTINUE'.

Each liveness signal is honoured INDEPENDENTLY, one arm per signal: output alone, a tool child alone (CPU flat), and CPU progress alone (no tool child) each keep the verdict CONTINUE past the silence window. The tool-child arm uses a tree where the only descendants are the shell and the provider process and asserts that does NOT count as a tool child.

The Windows probe is driven through its injectable runner in tests (no real process needed): a well-formed CIM answer yields OBSERVED with the summed CPU and the tool children below the provider; a failing, empty, malformed or timed-out runner yields UNKNOWN with a named reason, never OBSERVED and never a throw. One real-host arm, gated like apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts, probes the test runner's own pid on Windows and asserts OBSERVED.

Gate quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.test.ts`, plus `pnpm typecheck` (the daemon project now carries erasableSyntaxOnly, so the new module must be erasable).

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN, in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts only.

RULE 1:
- Add `let lastUnobservedAt = startedAt;`. In settle(), both unobserved branches set `lastUnobservedAt = at`: the no-probe branch (answer undefined, which also covers a pid of undefined) and the isProbeFailure branch.
- silentMs becomes `at - Math.max(lastActivityAt, lastUnobservedAt)`. stillness() reports its `since` from that same instant, so a kill line's "silent Xm" and its "since" agree.
- lastActivity() is unchanged, so the absolute-cap line still names the real last activity.
- Three texts state the old rule: the FAIL-CLOSED comment (:122), the `probe` option doc (:48, "judges on output alone") and the probeFailure doc (:55-58, "No liveness was granted for it"). Replace them with the new rule: a silence kill needs a whole window of ticks that SAW the tree still. A tick that could not see it is neither activity nor silence, and it restarts the count (epic rail 4: unverifiable evidence gains no authority). State the limits honestly: a probe that fails on every tick, or at least once in every window, leaves only the absolute cap, and one transient failure delays a kill by at most one window.

RULE 2:
- DELETE CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS together with its whole UNMEASURED block (:23-42), the `cpuActivityFloorMs` option (:45) and `const floor` (:97). The step-1 census found no consumer anywhere. Do not add another floor, rate or knob: the ruling says no per-interval number separates hung from working on this host.
- The growth test:
  - `cpuDelta > 0` is activity and reads `cpu +<growth>`;
  - `cpuDelta < 0` keeps its landed meaning: "cpu rebased (a process left the tree)", and it counts as activity;
  - exactly 0 reads "cpu unchanged";
  - undefined stays "cpu baseline taken".
  The activity condition becomes `cpuDelta !== undefined && cpuDelta !== 0`.
- The growth label: below one second, whole ms rounded UP (Math.ceil) followed by `ms`, so a real growth never reads as zero. From one second up, keep the landed `(ms / 1_000).toFixed(1)` followed by `s`. So 15.625 reads "16ms", 125 reads "125ms" and 1_300 reads "1.3s".
- Record the ruling in the file header, in place of the floor block:
  - CPU is evidence, never a threshold (human ruling 2026-09-18, task-eca3780d comment-6d395077).
  - Measured on this host through this probe, in ms of tree CPU per ~60 s (comment-a96f4b63): a hung `claude -p` burns 125-547; a working one with no tool child burns 219-1219.
  - The bands overlap, so any growth counts as activity, and a hung seat that still burns CPU is bounded only by the absolute cap.
  - The reason: a wasted wait is recoverable, but a killed working seat loses its context.
- Keep the header's launcher-chain blind-spot sentence (:16-18). It is still true.
